name: Purse Identity
abstract: Purse Identity, formerly ReachFive, is a SaaS, API-first customer identity and access management (CIAM) platform now part of Purse alongside its payment orchestration products. It combines authentication (password, social login, passkeys and FIDO2, passwordless by email magic link or SMS code), MFA by email or SMS with step-up and risk-based authentication, SSO and cross-domain sessions, and a consent and preference center with double opt-in and full traceability for GDPR. Fraud protection covers bots, credential stuffing, breached credentials, rate limiting and account lockout. It acts as a partially implemented OpenID Connect provider (authorization code with PKCE, implicit, ROPC, refresh tokens with rotation) and can act as an OpenID provider for partner sites. Delivered through hosted pages, JavaScript, iOS and Android SDKs, and a Management API. Pricing is quote-based.

features.description: Password authentication is supported through the Identity API and the JavaScript, iOS and Android SDKs, with a configurable password policy.

Social login is documented for Amazon, Apple, Facebook, Google (including One Tap), Instagram, LinkedIn, Microsoft, PayPal, TikTok, X, WeChat, Line, Kakao, Naver, QQ, Weibo, VKontakte, Yandex, FranceConnect and others. Custom identity providers can also be added.
Passkeys and FIDO2 biometric authentication are supported for passwordless login.
Passwordless sign-in by email magic link is configured in the console under Settings > Passwordless; the email template also exposes a verification code variable.
Passwordless sign-in by SMS verification code (6 digits by default). It is only activated when phone numbers are unique per user, and the docs call it a less secure approach.
Magic links are sent by email, or generated through the Management API /magic-link endpoint and embedded anywhere.

Risk-based authentication scores each login from 0 to 100 (default threshold 30) using trusted device, IP address, operating system and geolocation, and triggers an MFA step-up above the threshold. It must be enabled by Professional Services and does not work with the ROPC flow.
Not documented in Purse Identity's public documentation.
MFA step-up is supported for sensitive actions through the /identity/v1/mfa/stepup endpoint. MFA sessions last 1 to 720 hours (default 72).

Purse Identity is documented as a partially implemented OpenID Connect Provider: OAuth 2.0 authorization and token endpoints, ID tokens as JWT, discovery and a JWKS document. ID tokens are signed per client with HS256 (default) or RS256. The documentation does not say which parts of the protocol are missing.
